_readme: Every string, image path and icon name the `aluma` template renders. Aluma.jsx contains no copy of its own — rebranding the site is an edit to this file only. `icon` values are lucide-react export names, resolved through the ICONS table in Aluma.jsx; a name missing from that table renders no icon rather than crashing.

brand.name: Aluma
brand.documentTitle: Aluma — A Lakeside Retreat in the Northern Highlands

hero.heading: The lake keeps its own time
hero.body: Twenty-four rooms on a shoreline that has looked the same for four thousand years. No schedule, no clocks in the suites, and a boat waiting whenever you want one.

welcome.statement: Aluma began as a fishing cabin with three beds and a stove, built by a family who kept coming back to the same stretch of water. Fifty years later it is a retreat of twenty-four rooms, and it is still the same stretch of water.
body: The buildings are timber and glass, set low against the treeline so the shoreline reads as unbroken from the far bank. Nothing here is taller than the pines.

Everything is walkable: the sauna at the water's edge, the boathouse, the kitchen garden that supplies most of what arrives at your table. The nearest road is four kilometres behind you and you will not hear it.

suites.heading: Four ways to wake up here

items.name: Forest Suite
items.body: Set back into the pines, with a west-facing bed and a wood stove that is lit before you arrive. The darkest room on the property, deliberately.

items.name: Lake Suite
items.body: Full-height glass on the water side, four metres from the shore. In still weather the reflection reaches the foot of the bed.

items.name: Ridge Room
items.body: The highest room at Aluma, above the treeline on the northern slope. Cooler, quieter, and the only one that sees the far peaks.

items.name: The Boathouse
items.body: The original 1974 building, rebuilt around its own frame. A whole lodge to yourself, with a jetty, a sauna and a kitchen you are welcome to ignore.

experiences.heading: Things worth getting out of bed for

items.title: Cold water, warm wood
items.body: The sauna sits on the jetty for one reason. Sixteen minutes at ninety degrees, then eight metres to the ladder. Guided sessions at dusk, or take a key and go alone.

items.title: Walks with someone who knows
items.body: Four routes across the estate, from an hour along the shore to a full day over the ridge. Led by guides who grew up on this side of the lake.

items.title: The boats
items.body: Six wooden rowing boats and two small sailing dinghies, free to take out at any hour. The lake has no motor traffic and never has.

items.title: Dark skies
items.body: No settlement within forty kilometres. From September the aurora is a regular event, and there is a heated platform on the north shore for watching it.

valley.heading: Above the cloud line, most mornings
valley.body: Lake Sarven sits at 840 metres, in a basin the weather rarely reaches properly. Cloud gathers below the ridge and stays there, so the mornings tend to be clear from the property and grey from the valley floor.

points.title: Getting here
points.body: Two hours from the regional airport, the last forty minutes on estate road. We collect you.

points.title: The season
points.body: Open year-round. Swimming from May, aurora from September, ice on the shallows by January.

points.title: The estate
points.body: 1,400 acres held in a conservation trust since 1991. No development beyond the existing footprint, ever.

spa.heading: Heat, cold, and nothing to do in between
spa.body: Three saunas, a cold plunge cut into the rock, and a treatment room with one therapist and one appointment at a time. Bookable the same day, usually.

venues.name: Fen & Ash
venues.body: The main room. A set menu built each morning from whatever the garden, the lake and the two farms up the valley have given us.

venues.name: The Long Room
venues.body: Breakfast, lunch and everything in between, at a single oak table that seats thirty and rarely does. Come as you are, eat when you like.

venues.name: The Garden Kitchen
venues.body: Fire, vegetables and one long bench under the apple trees. The shortest supply chain we have: about nine metres.

items.quote: We booked three nights and changed our flights twice. By the last morning I could tell the weather from the sound of the water before opening the curtains, which is not a thing I knew was possible.
items.name: Ingrid Hallström

items.quote: The sauna-and-plunge ritual is the reason to come and the food is the reason to stay. Seven courses and not one of them was trying to impress me.
items.name: Tomás Reyes

items.quote: No clock in the room and no signal on the estate. I resented both for about four hours and then stopped noticing. Came back in the same year, which I never do.
items.name: Amara Osei

footer.blurb: A twenty-four room retreat on the north bank of Lake Sarven, held in conservation trust and run by the same family since 1974.

newsletter.title: Two letters a year
newsletter.body: What the season is doing, and when rooms open. Nothing else.
